_comment: What a remote fleet may launch in this repository. Read by an OrbitOrc agent out of this
checkout; nothing in this file is code and nothing here is evaluated.
The three modes below are the ones tools/netbench/bench.sh launches on ONE box. A fleet run puts
the server on one machine and the bot clients on others, which is the arrangement bench.sh cannot
produce: it conditions a loopback socket and every process contends for the same cores, so a
send-path cost measured there describes the harness. See docs/netbench.md.
PORTS. The defaults here are 47900/47910, deliberately clear of 47800/47810, which bench.sh and
the two-process gates bind. A run on this box must not make an unrelated CI probe fail to bind.
What a job here needs in order to mean anything, relative to the checkout. These are not where a
build lands -- they are what must already be present, and the native library is the one whose
absence ruins a run quietly: every class it registers resolves to nothing, so the project dies at
load or comes up empty and writes a full metrics file of zeros.
Which columns testify that a client actually simulated. An ALLOW-LIST on purpose: an
ignore-list would let a new transport counter rescue a run in which nothing simulated, which is
the exact answer the verdict exists to refuse. Every column here is a property of the locally
predicted body being reconciled against the server.
judged_modes holds only the modes that CAN move them. A dedicated server has no predicted body
and writes zeros by construction, so accusing it would be a false accusation.

events._comment: The demo prints one of these per state transition; the prefix differs per demo project.

_comment: The authority. ORBITNET_DEBUG=1 is the server-side measurement: every send-path column reads
zero in a client CSV because a client is not the authority and runs none of it. The backend
prints a per-second wire line under this variable, and that line is the only way a send-path
change can be compared at all.
quit-after is a backstop, not the measurement window. The window is the clients' own.
The conditioned link, and the honest conditioner: ENet ships none, and wrapping the peer would
sit above retransmit. It runs as a script rather than a session -- it builds no world -- and it
must outlive the whole run, because staggered client bringup pushes the last window well past
relay start.
A bot client. It drives the real input path through a BenchPolicy, streams per-tick metrics to
a CSV and self-evaluates on finish. Headless by request rather than by declaration: the same
mode is what a person drives on a machine with a display, and forcing headless is how a fleet
puts several on one box.
SEAT COUNT BOUNDS THE FLEET. This demo seats 24; a client past the seat count is admitted as an
observer, drives no body, and reports no samples -- which the measurement verdict then reads as
a run that measured nothing.

observer._comment: Watches without playing: no seat, no body, an interest center and a world declared by the server.

probe._comment: The automated arena gate: boot, membership, veto, resume. Runs headless in CI and on a box.
